decisions.issues: v02 is the only candidate offered, and it fixes the round-1 failure: the Dutch party now appears only at the far doorway. Everything the beat needs is there. Varma sits on the low platform in the court look (turban with peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, spear within reach, bare feet on the mat). Nagoji is the only man standing beside the platform, on the king's right, and matches his look: black topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, heavy silver chain with a round pendant, an ivory-handled knife at the waist of a plain cream mundu with no gold border, and a shoulder cloth. Ramayyan sits at the foot of the platform with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Padmini (with her stick) and Revathi (indigo, jasmine braid, armlets, no tali) sit on the left, and ministers sit on both sides. There is no painted text. The top-left rafters and sky, and the top-right rafters, leave room for both captions. Minor, all tolerable: (1) the grey streak at Nagoji's temple is a little stronger than 'a first touch'; (2) the doorway figures are hazy rather than fully featureless, and one of them wears his tricorne on his head; (3) Nagoji's lowered left hand is hidden behind Ramayyan's head, which makes a slight tangent; (4) Padmini's hair shows no grey threading.

v02 is the only candidate offered. The foreground beat is right. Lannoy stands at frame right, seen from behind, and matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, no wig, white tunic-coat over a white mundu, European sword with its hilt wrapped in local cloth. Two Nair guards (bare chest, white mundu, sword and round shield) stand at ease beside him. In the aisle, the senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, lace cuff) dips a stiff bow with his tricorne at his chest, and the younger envoy (own brown hair tied back, brown coat, hat in hand) stands open-mouthed. The round-1 background faults are fixed: no crown, no spear-bearer, no women on the platform, Nagoji standing on the king's right, and Padmini and Revathi seated on the left. The open sea side matches 2.1. There is no painted text. The sky and rafters above the envoys (upper left) and the plain back wall above the dais both leave clean room for the two balloons. Small residual background faults, each under about 40 px at frame scale: (1) Varma's face is younger, with only a thin moustache instead of the V13 thick curled one; (2) the bald man at the foot of the platform (Ramayyan's place) has a moustache and no curly hair at the sides; (3) Nagoji has a tiny white forehead dot, a gold border on his mundu and shoulder cloth (2.1 shows them plain), a pendant-style silver collar instead of the 2.1 chain, and an earring that reads as a tiny drop. These are candidates for retouching, not grounds for another regeneration.

Acceptable with minor deviations. The beat reads clearly: Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals, pale hair tied with a black ribbon, steps out at frame right. The senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne in hand), the younger envoy (brown hair, brown coat), the bareheaded grey-coated scribes and the interpreter (red-and-gold-bordered shoulder cloth) all face the platform. Varma sits still in the turban with the peacock-feather crest, eyes narrowed. Hall blocking matches pages 2 to 7: Nagoji is the only man standing, on the king's right, with a topknot, no turban, a silver chain, the ivory knife, a curled moustache, a clean chin and a gold ear ornament. Ramayyan sits at the foot of the platform, bald crown, clean-shaven, with leaves and stylus. Padmini and Revathi (indigo, jasmine) sit at the left, and the ministers sit at the right. There is no text, no gore and hands are sound. Minor points: Nagoji's grey temple streak is a little heavier than a first touch, though it matches the page-2 candidates. His mundu and shoulder cloth have gold borders, where the script asks for plain cloth. He wears gold armlets. Lannoy's sword hilt is bare gilt instead of wrapped in cloth. Two ministers wear gold chains. No spear is visible near Varma. The long caption fits the low-detail roof and rafter band across the top (y 0 to 0.09), or the top-left corner over the carved pillar, without covering a face.

Minor only: Nagoji's grey at the temple is a visible streak rather than a faint first touch; the angle on Varma is closer to eye level than a true low angle and his forward lean is slight; frame is landscape rather than tall. Otherwise clean: Nagoji at the king's right (viewer's left) with black topknot, no turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; Varma in cream-and-gold turban with peacock crest and spear upright; senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne in hand) back to us in the foreground with the younger envoy and interpreter; ministers murmuring on both sides; same open coastal hall as 4.1-4.3. No painted text. Lettering space: sky above and right of Varma's turban for Varma's lines, and the low-detail charcoal coat back (or sky) for the envoy's line.

Minor only. All four fixes from round 1 landed. The red runner and steps carry only plain woven stripes, with no glyphs. Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are plain cream with no gold border. His arms are clasped behind his back, so the inner left forearm is hidden. The inset shows Revathi's hand relaxed with the fingers open (gold armlet, bangles, indigo-and-gold border), so the fist reads as loosening. Varma matches varma-v1: cream-and-gold turban, jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, spear upright. Nagoji is at the king's right with a topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a gold ear stud and the ivory-handled knife. Remaining quibbles: (1) the grey at Nagoji's temple runs back along the side of his head, more than a 'first touch', as already accepted in 2.3; (2) his chain of office is drawn as a jewelled silver necklace, as accepted in 2.2; (3) he is a heavily muscled figure rather than lean. The envoys' costumes are correct (grey wig and charcoal coat, own brown hair and brown coat), the tricorne is held in hand, the lamp flames stand straight, and the hall is the open-sided carved-pillar hall. Lettering space for the three Varma lines is the rafters at the top right and the large dark backs of the two envoys at the bottom.

Acceptable, with one staging inconsistency. The round-1 failures are fixed. No one stands beside the king, so there is no Nagoji lookalike. The guards are far back in white headbands, and the seated ministers are bareheaded in plain white with no gold chains. Varma matches varma-v1 (turban, crest, gold necklaces, bare chest). His head and eyes are turned level to screen right, over the seated envoys toward the far side of the hall, and the senior envoy looks up at him with a clenched jaw and pressed lips. That is the swallow beat, though the jabot hides the throat itself. Remaining issues: (1) both envoys sit cross-legged on the mats, while in 6.2 and 7.1 they stand. A similar seated staging was accepted in 4.2, but readers may notice it on this page. (2) The left scribe writes on a small low writing board, which is close to the 'no tables' rule but harmless. (3) No spear is in reach, which this panel does not require. Envoy costumes are correct, the hall and lighting match 6.2, and the broad clear sky across the upper middle takes both balloons without touching a face.

Minor only. The round-1 failure is fixed: this is now a strip about Lannoy alone, with no platform, king, women, ministers or guards. Lannoy matches the v15b sheet and the ch16-23 row: pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig, white stand-collar tunic-coat, white mundu. He stands very straight against a carved tiger pillar on a laterite base at screen right. In the soft foreground at left, only the backs of the envoys show, in the correct locks: the senior's grey wig with black bow and charcoal coat, and the younger's own brown hair tied back with a brown coat. Remaining quibbles: (1) Lannoy's eyes go off to screen right, away from the envoys rather than 'past their shoulders', though it still reads as a fixed refusal to meet them; (2) the sword hilt is brass with a cloth knotted around it rather than a fully wrapped grip, and it hangs with no visible belt, as accepted in 7.1. The hall, brass open-wick lamps, sea view and daylight match 6.4. Both off-panel Varma balloons fit in the clear sky in the upper middle. Their tails run to the left frame edge, toward the platform side established in 6.4.

Acceptable. Small notes only. The golden late-afternoon light reads as 'later', but 7.1, 7.3 and 7.5 are in blue-sky daylight, so 7.5 jumps back to midday right after this panel. The cloth on Lannoy's sword hilt is red here and white in 7.5, and no belt is visible holding the scabbard. Everything else matches: Lannoy fits his sheet (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, ankle-length mundu, sandals, hands clasped behind his back) and stands by a carved pillar at frame right. The senior envoy has his grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, thin lace cuffs and tricorne at his chest, and has stopped beside Lannoy, centre-left. Bare-chested Nair guards with sword and round shield lead the younger envoy (brown coat, his own hair), two grey-coated scribes and the interpreter toward frame left. Background chiefs walk off in pairs and the platform is empty. It is the same open coastal hall seen in the neighbouring panels. I found no text (the scribe's book is blank), no blood and no anachronism, and the hands are sound. Clear sky between the pillars, above both heads, has room for the envoy's balloon (upper centre-left) and Lannoy's (upper centre-right) without covering a face.

Clean. The framing now matches the beat: a tight insert from Nagoji's point of view on Revathi's throat. Flat gold coin discs, not round beads, fill the centre and catch the low sun. Only her lips and jaw show at the top edge, with no eyes and no repeat of the 8.2 portrait. The jasmine braid, jhumka and gold armlet match 8.2. The sari is indigo with a gold border and there is no tali. The verandah post, rail, palms and sunset sea are in the same light as 8.2. The face entry covers only her partial lower face (mouth and jaw), so the caption is kept off it. The warm sky above the sea at upper right, about x 0.68 to 1.0 and y 0.02 to 0.22, is clear for the one caption.

The r1 failures are fixed. Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are now plain cream with no gold border. His chain is now a round-link silver chain with a small round pendant. Minor issues remain, none disqualifying. The brand on his inner left forearm is a small brownish ring or rosette-like mark, placed mid-forearm nearer the elbow, next to the long white scar. It is a little more defined than a shapeless patch, but it is tiny at panel scale, has no letters and is not a cross. The chain is lighter than the heavier silver chain in 8.1. Padmini shows somewhat more grey than 'a few threads', but her hair is still mostly black and coiled at the nape. Everything else matches. Padmini walks in from frame left with her long stick, in a cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. Nagoji has a black topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small gold stud and the ivory knife at his waist, with his left hand on the rail. Revathi wears indigo with flat coins, jasmine braid, armlets and bangles. It is the same verandah and sunset as 8.1 to 8.3. All hands are sound. Balloon space: Padmini's medium balloon fits over the roof eaves at top left, and Nagoji's and Revathi's short balloons fit in the open sky at top centre and right.

Clean. The r1 failure is fixed. The brand is now a pale, shiny, puckered patch of raised ridges just above the wrist, with no shape, symbol, letters or cross. The long thin white scar runs from it toward the elbow. The cloth at frame right is plain cream with no gold edge. Revathi's bangled hand enters from frame left, and her fingertips brush the back of Nagoji's hand on the rail. His hand reads as a LEFT hand: back of the hand up, four fingers over the rail edge, thumb tucked on the far side. His nails are darkened and slightly ridged. A fold of gold-patterned indigo sari sits at frame left. Finger counts and anatomy are sound, and there is no pseudo-text. The verandah post, rail and sunset sea match 8.4. The open sky across the top is clear for both captions.

v02 (the only eligible candidate; v01 was rejected in r1) fixes all three r1 faults. Revathi now wears her fitted short-sleeved blue blouse with the armlets over the sleeves. Nagoji's chin is much cleaner. The stray marks on his outer left arm are gone. Faces, hands, Padmini with her stick, the sunset verandah and the open sky for balloons are all good. But Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth have broad gold kasavu borders: a gold stripe runs down the front of the mundu and a broad gold band runs along the shoulder cloth. The chapter 18 look note (repeated in the ch17 and ch19 scripts) locks a plain cream mundu with NO gold border and warns against copying the gold-bordered later-life figure on the sheet. In r1, 8.4 was rejected for exactly this. 8.1, on the same verandah minutes earlier, shows him in plain cream, so this would be a costume change in the middle of the scene. Minor: there is no grey at the temples (8.1 and 9.3 show a touch), and faint stubble-like dots remain on the jaw.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition and everything that now works: the sunset verandah, sea and palms; Padmini at the left with her walking stick, watching them; Revathi at the rail in her fitted short-sleeved deep-blue blouse, with the armlets over the sleeve hems, the flat-coin necklace, the jasmine braid and her open-handed gesture; and Nagoji leaning on the rail with clasped hands, with his high black topknot, flush gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, silver plaque chain with round medallion and ivory-handled knife. Fix his clothes. The mundu and the shoulder cloth are PLAIN cream cotton with NO gold border, NO gold kasavu stripe and no coloured stripe anywhere: not on the hem, the front fold or the edge of the shoulder cloth. This matches 8.1 on the same verandah. The gold-bordered cloth on the LATER LIFE figure of his sheet belongs to his old age and must not be copied. Add only a first light touch of grey at the temple above his ear and keep the rest of the hair black. Keep his chin and jaw smooth and fully clean-shaven, with no stubble dots, and keep his arms free of marks.

decisions.correction: Keep this exact night room, camera angle and lighting: the clay oil lamp at front left on its brass tray, the low writing board with faint-stroke sheets, the small brass ink pot, the woven mat, the window with night palms at left, the lit doorway at right, and Nagoji sitting cross-legged and writing, with his large shadow on the plain wall. Keep his flush gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, black topknot and silver plaque chain with round medallion. Fix his clothes. decisions.issues: Clean and on-script. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, striped shoulder cloth. He is seated and looking toward Nagoji, and the scar runs from his anatomical left ear to the jaw on the lamp side, facing us. Nagoji is in the near foreground with his back to us: black topknot with curls falling behind (as on the later-life sheet), a slight grey streak at the temple (fine for ch18), gold ear stud, curled moustache tip, cream shoulder cloth. His hair hides the silver chain from this angle, which is acceptable. The setting matches 10.1: lattice window, palm-leaf bundles, a brass lamp, the open doorway to the night. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Lettering space: the plain wall above and to the left of Ibrahim's turban, the upper lattice, and the dark doorway at top right.

Clean and on-script. Ibrahim is standing by a lit lamp. His brass cup is set down on the round stool, the same stool and cup that appear in 10.4. Behind him is the open door to the night with palms. He matches his sheet (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, vest pockets), and the scar is on his anatomical left, ear to jaw. Hands are sound: one fist at the vest, one open palm. There is no painted text on the bundles or door. Minor: the lamp is wall-mounted here but a standing lamp in 10.2, which is acceptable. Ibrahim's eyes turn to image-left, where Nagoji sits in 10.2 and 10.4, so the off-panel NAGOJI tail goes to the left edge. His open-hand gesture to the right reads as pointing at the night outside. The large plain wall on the right is ample lettering space.
